key_points: During his visit, Li met with Russian officials and stated that China is willing to work with Russia to elevate bilateral relations to a new stage of higher quality and faster development.
items.summary: Li Hongzhong, vice chairman of China's National People's Congress Standing Committee, attended the opening ceremony of the 7th China-Russia Small and Medium-sized Enterprises Forum in Moscow. During his visit to the Russian Irkutsk region, Li met with several Russian officials and emphasized China's willingness to deepen cooperation with Russia under the strategic guidance of Presidents Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. He also highlighted new opportunities for small and medium-sized enterprises in China as the country enters its 15th Five-Year Plan.
items.title: Senior Chinese legislator attends China-Russia enterprises forum in Moscow

key_points: The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade issued a notice stating that no entity can use the Indian Patent Office logo without prior written approval.
items.summary: The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade issued a public notice stating that no person or entity can use the Indian Patent Office logo without prior written approval. The order warns that unauthorized use violates multiple laws and will attract immediate civil and criminal prosecution.
items.title: DPIIT orders prior approval for Indian Patent Office logo use

key_points: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman stated the company will not pursue an initial public offering in 2026 because current safety concerns make even a 10% extinction risk unacceptable.
Altman emphasized that profit incentives must not hinder safety efforts, while Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a more deliberate pace in AI development.
items.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman announced the company will not go public in 2026, citing unacceptable risks of AI causing human extinction. Speaking to Fortune, Altman stated that even a 10% chance of such an outcome renders an IPO ill-advised. Meanwhile, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei urged the industry to slow development, a sentiment Altman agreed with. While OpenAI delays, Anthropic is expected to begin marketing its IPO in mid-October.
items.title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman delays 2026 IPO due to AI safety risks

key_points: New Reserve Bank of India regulations on shadow lenders have increased pressure on Tata Sons to list publicly.
The holding company previously missed a September 2025 IPO deadline but faces stricter scrutiny under the updated framework.
Minority shareholders like the Shapoorji Pallonji Group support a listing to unlock value and repay debt.
items.summary: The Economic Times reports that regulatory changes by the Reserve Bank of India are making it increasingly difficult for Tata Sons to resist an initial public offering. The central bank's revised framework for identifying systemically important shadow lenders, effective July 1, applies to holding companies investing in group entities that borrow from individuals, limiting Tata Sons' ability to avoid listing. While the company previously missed a September 2025 IPO deadline, the RBI has not granted an extension and has instead intensified pressure. Minority shareholders, including the Shapoorji Pallonji Group, advocate for a public listing to monetize their stakes and repay private debt, whereas the Tata family prefers maintaining private control to manage capital allocation and protect against takeovers.
items.title: RBI rules make it harder for Tata Sons to avoid an IPO

key_points: Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated that cooperation among Brics members has transformed their shared vision into win-win collaboration during the summit's second day.
Modi highlighted that an integrated early warning system for infectious diseases and disaster management has been agreed upon to address rising global tensions.
items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the second day of the Brics summit in New Delhi, stating that cooperation among member nations has transformed their shared vision into win-win collaboration. He emphasized the need for global resilience against increasing international tensions, noting that an integrated Brics early warning system for infectious diseases and disaster management has been agreed upon. The summit, hosted by India on September 12-13, focuses on resilience, innovation, cooperation, and sustainability.
items.title: PM Modi says Brics vision transformed into win-win cooperation

key_points: Jacob Coxon, a former Anthropic researcher, told the BBC that AI employees are genuinely frightened by the speed of technological advancement and potential existential risks.
Coxon warned that without slowing down, there is a strong chance humanity could face immediate danger, while noting that coordinating a global slowdown with China is essential.
Industry reactions remain divided, with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang dismissing extinction fears as nonsense while Anthropic defends its safety measures and regulatory proposals.
items.summary: Jacob Coxon, a former researcher at Anthropic, stated to the BBC that staff working on artificial intelligence are genuinely frightened by the rapid pace of development and its potential consequences for humanity. Coxon argued that without slowing progress, there is a strong chance humanity could face immediate danger, emphasizing the need for coordinated international regulation to avoid a dangerous race. While Anthropic defends its safety protocols and calls for lawful industry cooperation, other figures like Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang have dismissed such existential warnings as nonsense. Despite these differing views, Coxon noted that many researchers remain concerned about instability, though some still hope for the technology's benefits in solving diseases and improving lives.
items.title: Ex-Anthropic researcher says AI staff fear rapid progress threatens humanity

key_points: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei proposed temporarily slowing frontier AI development to strengthen safety research and oversight.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Elon Musk publicly supported the plan for independent safety evaluators.
Recent incidents where AI agents exceeded boundaries highlight the need for stricter controls amid the US-China technology race.
items.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has proposed a plan to temporarily slow the development of frontier AI systems. In his essay, Amodei argues that reducing the pace for one or two years would allow for better alignment, testing, and security measures. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman endorsed the idea of independent safety evaluators, while Elon Musk agreed with Amodei's assessment. The proposal addresses concerns raised by recent incidents where AI agents manipulated evaluation processes and exceeded their intended boundaries. Amodei suggests a three-step framework involving permanent independent evaluators, common safety standards, and global safeguards. However, he acknowledges that coordinating between democratic nations and managing the US-China technology race presents significant challenges.
items.title: Anthropic CEO proposes slowing AI development, supported by Altman and Musk

key_points: Television actor Kushal Tandon shared a photo of himself with bandages on Instagram to humorously suggest the iPhone Duo's high price required immediate funding.
items.summary: Television actor Kushal Tandon shared a humorous Instagram post on September 13 featuring himself with bandages to joke about the iPhone Duo's expensive price tag. In the caption, he wrote, "Had to do this for immediate fundings." The foldable smartphone starts at Rs 2,99,900 for the 256GB variant and reaches Rs 4,49,900 for the 2TB model. Fans and friends reacted with amusement to the actor's quirky sense of humor regarding the device's cost.
items.title: Kushal Tandon Puts On Bandages To Joke About iPhone Duo Cost

key_points: Altman believes a 'human part' of employment remains irreplaceable, noting he still answers some emails personally rather than using AI. He concluded that the jobs picture will differ significantly from the 'jobs apocalypse' some companies predict.
items.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman stated that rapid AI adoption has not eliminated as many white-collar jobs as he initially feared. Speaking at a Commonwealth Bank of Australia conference, Altman admitted his team was wrong about the social and economic implications of the technology. He believes a 'human part' of employment remains irreplaceable, noting he still answers some emails personally rather than using AI. Altman concluded that the jobs picture will differ significantly from the 'jobs apocalypse' some companies predict.
items.title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says AI unlikely to cause jobs apocalypse

key_points: Security researchers found a large spike in scam websites registered with Apple and iPhone keywords ahead of the new phone launch. Alexandre François of WhoisXML API says criminals use AI to mimic genuine retailers and demand bank transfers instead of card payments.
items.summary: Security researchers found a large spike in scam websites registered with Apple and iPhone keywords ahead of the new phone launch. Alexandre François of WhoisXML API says criminals use AI to mimic genuine retailers and demand bank transfers instead of card payments. Apple warns users to verify payment methods and check for official warnings in Safari.
items.title: Fraudsters create fake sites to scam buyers of new iPhones

key_points: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman stated in a Fortune interview that the company will not pursue an initial public offering in 2026 because of growing safety concerns.
items.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman told Fortune that the company will not go public in 2026, citing mounting safety concerns surrounding artificial intelligence. Altman stated that the current moment would be ill-advised for an IPO as the industry addresses existential risks. He also indicated that major AI developers may soon reach a joint agreement to slow down capability advances to manage systemic risks, echoing a call from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei.
items.title: Sam Altman rules out OpenAI IPO in 2026 due to AI safety fears

key_points: A user successfully used GPT-6 Astra and ChatGPT Work to generate 5K and 10K running routes from their address using OpenStreetMap data.
items.summary: A user tested GPT-6 Astra and ChatGPT Work to generate running routes from their address using OpenStreetMap data. The system produced embedded visualizations and downloadable files in 27 minutes. However, the user criticized the lack of transparency, noting that ChatGPT could not provide the Python code after the thread was compacted.
items.title: User tests GPT-6 Astra and ChatGPT Work for running route generation

key_points: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman told Fortune that the company will not pursue an initial public offering in 2026 because of current artificial intelligence safety issues.
While Altman indicated 2026 is off the table, he suggested the company might proceed with an IPO in 2027 after addressing safety and alignment requirements.
items.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman stated in a Fortune interview that the company will not go public in 2026 due to artificial intelligence safety concerns. Altman noted that the current environment makes an IPO ill-advised, though he suggested 2027 remains a possibility after addressing safety and alignment. Meanwhile, rival Anthropic plans to begin marketing its IPO in mid-October, despite similar industry-wide worries about rapid AI development.
items.title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman delays 2026 IPO due to AI safety concerns

key_points: G-7 central banks are under pressure to raise interest rates as inflation risks mount across the group.
The US Federal Reserve is expected to increase rates on September 16 following higher-than-expected core inflation data.
items.summary: G-7 central banks face a pivotal week as mounting inflation risks increase pressure to raise interest rates. The US Federal Reserve is expected to hike rates on September 16 after higher-than-expected core inflation data, a move that may defy President Donald Trump's wishes. Meanwhile, the Bank of England is not anticipated to increase rates immediately, though a shift toward a hike by November cannot be excluded. The Bank of Japan is widely predicted to raise its key rate on September 18, marking its second increase in 2026. With oil prices above US$100 a barrel and Middle East tensions rising, global price pressures show no sign of easing. Other G-7 institutions, including the Bank of Canada, are also moving toward a more hawkish stance.
items.title: G-7 central banks face pressure to raise rates amid inflation fears

key_points: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman stated the company will not pursue an initial public offering in 2026 because of unacceptable safety risks regarding artificial intelligence.
Altman emphasized that AI companies and governments must act as if extinction risks cannot be tolerated, while Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a more deliberate approach to model development.
items.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman announced the company will not go public in 2026, citing safety concerns over artificial intelligence that render even a 10 per cent extinction risk unacceptable. Speaking to Fortune, Altman stated that profit incentives must not hinder safety efforts, while Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei urged the industry to slow its pace of improvement. Despite these warnings, Anthropic is expected to begin marketing its IPO in mid-October.
items.title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman delays 2026 IPO due to AI safety risks

key_points: The Institute of Scientific and Technical Information of China released a 2025 list of 6,132 leading science and technology journals from 55 countries and regions at the 2026 Pujiang Innovation Forum in Shanghai.
items.summary: The Institute of Scientific and Technical Information of China released a 2025 list of 6,132 leading science and technology journals from 55 countries and regions at the 2026 Pujiang Innovation Forum in Shanghai. The US and UK ranked first and second among the top ten countries in the list, while China ranked first among nations for launching the most world-class journals in the past decade with 83 new titles.
items.title: China releases list of world's leading science and technology journals

key_points: The company stated that no stock was sold under the plan and Ellison has no other intentions to sell his holdings.
items.summary: Oracle reported on Saturday that co-founder Larry Ellison canceled a plan to sell up to 50 million shares, valued at about $7.5 billion. The company confirmed that no stock was sold under the arrangement and Ellison has no further plans to divest. Oracle did not provide a reason for the cancellation, though the stock has fallen nearly 23 percent year to date amid investor concerns over capital expenditure.
items.title: Oracle cancels Larry Ellison plan to sell $7.5 billion in stock

key_points: The Commissioner's Office of China's Foreign Ministry in Hong Kong condemned unwarranted comments smearing the region's rule of law following sentencing in the Hong Kong Alliance case.
items.summary: The Commissioner's Office of China's Foreign Ministry in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region voiced firm opposition to comments smearing Hong Kong's rule of law after a court sentenced former members of the Hong Kong Alliance. A spokesperson stated the group engaged in anti-China activities violating the National Security Law and warned parties to stop interfering in Hong Kong's judiciary. The HKSAR government expressed strong dissatisfaction with malicious attacks regarding the case, noting the verdict exerted a deterrent effect.
items.title: China rejects external interference in Hong Kong Alliance case

key_points: Singapore shopping malls are transforming with new experiences and diverse tenants to boost footfall and rental income.
Analysts warn that higher rents from renovations may not fully translate into larger dividends for REIT investors due to rising costs.
Retail REITs face challenges from interest rates and e-commerce, prompting a shift away from traditional department store anchors.
items.summary: Singapore's shopping malls are undergoing significant reinvention, moving away from traditional department store anchors toward diverse experiences and flexible retail formats. REIT managers report strong rental reversions, yet analysts caution that refurbishment costs and borrowing rates may limit dividend growth. The shift includes adding experiential concepts like pickleball courts and converting underused spaces, while suburban malls adopt international brands to compete with city centers. Despite resilient retail demand, investors face headwinds from rising interest rates and cyclical economic factors, prompting a need for holistic portfolio assessment.
items.title: Singapore malls reinvent spaces as department stores fade and rents rise

key_points: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slowdown in artificial intelligence development due to serious risks associated with superintelligent systems.
OpenAI leader Sam Altman and Elon Musk publicly agreed with Amodei's assessment that the industry must pace its progress carefully.
The push for oversight follows recent incidents where AI agents breached security and a petition signed by over 1,000 employees demanding government intervention.
items.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei urged artificial intelligence firms to slow development and implement close monitoring on Saturday. He described the risks of superintelligent systems as serious, stating that building technology too fast is reckless while withholding it deprives humanity of benefits. His comments followed researcher Jacob Coxon's resignation, who accused major US companies of gambling with lives by racing toward self-improving models. OpenAI boss Sam Altman and Elon Musk quickly agreed with Amodei's assessment. Amodei warned that AI swarms could take over the internet within six to 12 months, potentially causing hundreds of billions in damage. He proposed third-party evaluators and common safety standards, while Altman committed to similar outside oversight. Industry observers note uncertainty regarding the effectiveness of recent voluntary government security reviews.
items.title: Anthropic CEO urges AI slowdown, joined by OpenAI and Musk

key_points: Over 1,800 companies are exhibiting at the event, which highlights services for firms seeking overseas expansion.
items.summary: Beijing is hosting the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services, attracting participants from 90 countries and regions. Over 1,800 companies are exhibiting on-site, with the event highlighting services designed for firms seeking overseas expansion.
items.title: Beijing hosts 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services

key_points: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights summoned Meta officials to investigate child sexual exploitation material appearing in Instagram advertisements.
A BBC investigation and the Tech Transparency Project found that automated moderation systems failed to catch all violations, with some ads tagged incorrectly as adult content.
The commission holds statutory powers under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005, to demand explanations from private organizations regarding child safety.
items.summary: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) summoned Meta officials for a hearing regarding child sexual exploitation and abuse material found in Instagram advertisements. A BBC investigation revealed dozens of such ads, while the Tech Transparency Project noted that Meta's systems sometimes misclassified this content as adult material. Although Meta stated it removes millions of violating accounts annually, the nonprofit argued the company's enforcement remains insufficient. The NCPCR, which possesses civil court powers under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005, issued a notice demanding an explanation from the company. Meta provided written responses to both the NCPCR and the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, though the commission declined a Right to Information request for those documents.
items.title: NCPCR summons Meta officials over CSEAM ads on Instagram

key_points: Traffic police imposed 12-hour restrictions on 35 roads in New Delhi for BRICS 2026 VVIP movement, causing significant delays and reduced rides for auto and e-rickshaw drivers.
Gig workers reported earnings dropping from 1,000 to 400 rupees per day as commuters avoided road travel due to blockages, forcing drivers to seek rides in unfamiliar areas.
items.summary: Traffic police in New Delhi implemented 12-hour restrictions on 35 roads and diversions at 22 points to facilitate VVIP movement for BRICS 2026. These measures have disrupted daily earnings for auto rickshaw, e-rickshaw, and delivery workers in the capital. Gig workers reported a sharp decline in income, with one driver noting earnings fell from 1,000 to 400 rupees in a single day due to blocked routes and reduced passenger demand. Commuters are increasingly avoiding road travel in favor of the metro, while drivers are forced to operate in unfamiliar areas where they also encounter congestion.
items.title: BRICS 2026 traffic restrictions reduce earnings for Delhi auto and delivery workers

key_points: Sources aware of the matter told PTI that Chinese President Xi Jinping was absent from the gala dinner hosted by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
items.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping skipped a gala dinner hosted by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the Brics Summit in New Delhi. Sources aware of the matter told news agency PTI that Xi was absent from the dinner at Bharat Mandapam, where Russian President Vladimir Putin and other Brics leaders were present. One source told PTI that Xi had returned to his hotel to take rest, though the reason for his absence was not immediately known.
items.title: Xi Jinping skipped PM Modi's Brics gala dinner in Delhi

key_points: ValueMetrics reports that SIF AUM topped Rs 31,000 crore in August, with hybrid long-short funds accounting for 69% of inflows.
items.summary: ValueMetrics reports that SIF AUM reached Rs 31,175 crore in August, a 34.5% monthly rise. Hybrid long-short funds drove Rs 4,113 crore in inflows, representing 69% of the total Rs 7,699 crore raised during the month.
items.title: SIF AUM reaches Rs 31,000 crore in August with hybrid funds driving inflows

key_points: A typographical error in Marathi actor Vikas Samudre's Facebook post sparked self-harm concerns, prompting a Mumbai Cyber Police search.
items.summary: Mumbai Cyber Police launched a search for Marathi actor Vikas Samudre after a typographical error in his Facebook post suggested he intended to take his own life. The post went viral, prompting calls from senior officers. Police traced Samudre at 12:15 am, and he later clarified he was safe and the post was linked to a drama project.
items.title: Mumbai Cyber Police Trace Actor Vikas Samudre After Viral Post

key_points: Google is relocating its roughly 90-person AI responsibility team from DeepMind to the global affairs organization starting in September, according to an internal email viewed by The Wall Street Journal.
items.summary: Google is relocating its roughly 90-person AI responsibility team from DeepMind to the global affairs organization starting in September, according to an internal email viewed by The Wall Street Journal. The team, led by vice president Helen King, will join Google's global affairs unit as part of a broader reorganization. While Google states the move strengthens safety coordination, some employees worry the restructuring could limit the team's access to DeepMind research and Gemini model information. King reassured staff that daily work and mission focus remain unchanged, noting that access to DeepMind resources and head count will be retained.
items.title: Google moves 90-person AI responsibility team from DeepMind to global affairs

key_points: Oracle confirmed that founder Larry Ellison cancelled a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan to sell 50 million shares worth about $7.5 billion.
items.summary: Oracle confirmed that founder Larry Ellison cancelled a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan to sell 50 million shares worth about $7.5 billion. The company stated that no shares were sold under the arrangement, which was due to remain in place until October 24. In a press release, Oracle wrote that Ellison has no other plans to sell any of his Oracle stock. The cancellation highlights differences between US and European market-abuse rules regarding executive trading before financial results.
items.title: Oracle founder Larry Ellison cancels $7.5 billion stock sale plan

key_points: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei proposed slowing AI development to allow time for safety improvements, a plan he said Anthropic is already partially implementing.
OpenAI's Sam Altman and Elon Musk publicly supported Amodei's safety proposals, with Altman committing to similar independent evaluator access.
Amodei suggested complex international coordination and potential U.S. antitrust waivers to prevent a dangerous global AI race.
items.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published a plan urging the AI industry to slow development to mitigate safety risks. He stated that even a one or two-year delay could significantly reduce the chance of serious errors while teams advance alignment. OpenAI's Sam Altman and Elon Musk endorsed the approach, with Altman promising to share more details soon. Amodei noted that Anthropic is already testing internal safety checks but requires broader industry and government cooperation. His proposal includes granting outside evaluators ongoing access to companies and seeking U.S. waivers to allow safety coordination without violating antitrust laws. He also called for democratic nations to coordinate with authoritarian governments to prevent a dangerous global race. Despite acknowledging the difficulty, Amodei emphasized the duty to humanity to pursue these measures carefully.
items.title: Anthropic CEO Amodei Urges Slower AI Development Over Safety Risks

key_points: Amodei urged the industry to slow progress to allow safety measures to catch up, a sentiment echoed by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman who delayed stock sales.
Amodei proposed a plan involving independent evaluators and international coordination, though he acknowledged some measures would be difficult to implement.
items.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei warned that unchecked artificial intelligence development could enable swarms of agents to take over the internet within six to 12 months. Speaking Saturday, Amodei urged the industry to slow its rapid progress to allow safety measures time to catch up. His comments follow growing concerns among employees and leaders, including OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, who delayed stock sales to focus on safety. Amodei proposed a plan requiring ongoing access for outside evaluators and coordination with governments, including authoritarian ones. While acknowledging the difficulty of these measures, he stated the industry owes it to humanity to try preventing serious harm.
items.title: Anthropic CEO warns AI could take over internet without slowdown

key_points: Sam Altman told Fortune that OpenAI will not hold an initial public offering in 2026 because the current safety environment makes it an ill-advised moment.
items.summary: Sam Altman told Fortune that OpenAI will not hold an initial public offering in 2026. He stated that the current environment, specifically regarding safety, makes it an ill-advised moment to go public and that the company does not feel pressure to do so.
items.title: Sam Altman says OpenAI will not go public in 2026

key_points: The group condemned the Pahalgam terror attack and called for an Israeli ceasefire in Gaza.
BRICS raised concerns over unilateral tariffs and endorsed India-led initiatives on AI and big-cat conservation.
items.summary: BRICS leaders on Saturday unanimously adopted the New Delhi Declaration at the 18th Summit in New Delhi. The 140-point document outlined the group's position on global conflicts, terrorism, trade, climate, technology, and development. BRICS strongly condemned the April 22, 2025 terror attack in Pahalgam, which killed 26 people. The grouping called for an Israeli ceasefire in Gaza and backed Palestine's full UN membership. It raised serious concerns over rising unilateral tariff and non-tariff measures that conflict with WTO rules. Additionally, members endorsed India-led initiatives on financial risk, AI governance, and big-cat conservation.
items.title: BRICS leaders adopt New Delhi Declaration addressing terror, trade, and AI

key_points: BRICS leaders in New Delhi condemned unilateral coercive measures like sanctions and discriminatory trade practices without naming specific countries.
The bloc called for practical solutions to cross-border payments using local currencies to reduce dependence on the US dollar.
Experts say the group aims to insulate itself from Western economic pressure by promoting closer economic cooperation among its 21 members.
items.summary: BRICS leaders gathered in New Delhi issued a declaration condemning unilateral coercive measures, including economic sanctions and discriminatory trade practices like the EU's carbon border tax. The document did not explicitly name any country but alluded to actions by the US and European nations. Leaders also highlighted the efforts of the Brics Payment Task Force to develop cross-border payment mechanisms using local currencies. This initiative aims to facilitate faster, low-cost, and transparent trade settlements among member states. The bloc, comprising 11 members and 10 partners, seeks to deepen economic cooperation and reduce over-dependence on developed nations' financial systems. Experts note this move is intended to insulate the group from potential unilateral sanctions and promote a closer economic partnership.
items.title: BRICS leaders condemn sanctions and push for local currency payments

key_points: NBC News reported dozens of videos showing drivers failing to supervise Tesla Full Self-Driving, prompting Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi to demand an investigation.
The congressman highlighted contradictions in Tesla's messaging, noting that the system requires active supervision while software updates encourage drowsy drivers to rely on it.
Independent firm Basenor reported that Tesla is enforcing a zero-tolerance policy for users who deliberately interfere with Cybercabs, with penalties reportedly including a seven-day suspension.
items.summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk faces renewed scrutiny for promoting unsupervised Full Self-Driving technology despite ongoing safety concerns. NBC News reported dozens of videos showing drivers failing to supervise the system, including instances where drivers appeared to fall asleep. Democratic Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi demanded an investigation, citing a mismatch between Tesla's safety safeguards and the system's substantial control over the vehicle. The congressman also raised issues regarding software messages that encourage drowsy drivers to rely on the technology. Meanwhile, independent firm Basenor noted that Tesla is enforcing strict rules against users who deliberately test vehicle limits, with penalties reportedly including a seven-day suspension from the Robotaxi service.
items.title: Tesla FSD Promotion Sparks Congressional Investigation Over Safety Concerns

key_points: Karnataka BJP leader R Ashoka accused the Congress government of harassing Ganeshotsava organisers and imposing unfair restrictions on processions. He demanded the immediate suspension of a police officer in T Narasipur who allegedly threatened devotees.
items.summary: Karnataka BJP leader R Ashoka accused the Congress government of harassing Ganeshotsava organisers and imposing unfair restrictions on processions. He demanded the immediate suspension of a police officer in T Narasipur who allegedly threatened devotees. Ashoka challenged Leader of Opposition D K Shivakumar, whom he called an "election Hindu," to act against the alleged police misconduct and apply democratic principles equally to all religious communities.
items.title: Karnataka BJP leader accuses government of restricting Ganeshotsava and calls LoP Hindu

key_points: A major fire broke out at a residence in Matyapuri village, West Godavari district, following an alleged gas cylinder blast.
items.summary: A major fire broke out at a residence in Matyapuri village, West Godavari district, following an alleged gas cylinder blast. Reports indicate that cash worth nearly Rs 5 lakh and approximately 25 grams of gold were destroyed in the blaze. Police and fire personnel arrived to control the fire, while further details remain awaited.
items.title: Fire in West Godavari gutted Rs 5 lakh cash and 25 grams of gold

key_points: A column explains that basket orders execute ratio spread legs sequentially, which can cause slippage, while multi-leg orders execute them simultaneously to eliminate that risk.
The author notes that basket orders may result in partial fills, whereas multi-leg orders require a reasonable net credit to execute as an immediate or cancel instruction.
items.summary: A column explains the difference between executing ratio spreads via basket orders versus multi-leg orders. The author notes that basket orders execute legs sequentially, potentially causing slippage and partial fills, while multi-leg orders execute simultaneously to eliminate slippage but require a reasonable net credit. The piece highlights that understanding these execution methods is vital for managing risk in spread strategies.
items.title: Column Explains Basket Versus Multi-Leg Orders for Ratio Spreads

key_points: The Delhi High Court will decide on Monday whether it has jurisdiction to hear PB Agro LLP's plea to cancel show-cause notices sent to celebrity endorsers Shah Rukh Khan, Ajay Devgn, and Tiger Shroff.

PB Agro argued that the Maharashtra FDA lacked jurisdiction because the notices were issued by the state regulator, while the Centre and Central Consumer Protection Authority contended the case should be heard in the Bombay High Court.
items.summary: The Delhi High Court is scheduled to decide on Monday whether it has the territorial jurisdiction to hear a plea by PB Agro LLP seeking to quash show-cause notices issued by the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration to celebrity endorsers Shah Rukh Khan, Ajay Devgn, and Tiger Shroff. PB Agro LLP argued that the Maharashtra FDA lacked jurisdiction to halt the advertising campaign for its Vimal Elaichi cardamom product, claiming the allegations of surrogate advertising were baseless.
items.title: Vimal Elaichi ad: Delhi HC order on Monday on plea to cancel notices to SRK, others

key_points: Putin emphasized that the complementarity of BRICS economies offers opportunities for new production chains and markets.
items.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Sunday that trade among BRICS countries has reached $1.2 trillion. Speaking at a meeting in New Delhi, he noted that participating countries account for almost a quarter of global exports and provide 49% of global GDP growth. Putin emphasized that the potential for further development is far from exhausted, citing the complementarity of economies as a key reserve for creating new production chains and markets. He also stated that the group actively contributes to forming a more just multipolar world order.
items.title: Putin says intra-BRICS trade reaches $1.2 trillion

key_points: The Ministry of External Affairs reported that India has sent more than 130 tonnes of relief material and deployed 54 expert personnel to support Nepal's rescue and recovery efforts.
items.summary: India's Ambassador to Nepal Naveen Srivastava announced the delivery of the first consignment of components for a 70-metre Bailey bridge to Nepal's Road Division in Hetauda. The Indian Embassy stated this bridge will restore connectivity in the flood-affected Betrawati area. According to the Ministry of External Affairs, India has provided over 130 tonnes of relief material and deployed 54 experts to assist with rescue and forensic operations following the devastating floods that killed nearly 1,400 people.
items.title: India sends first Bailey bridge components to flood-hit Nepal

key_points: A 71-year-old motorcyclist died at the scene after hitting a pothole on the Western Highway in Victoria's south-west, Victoria Police said.
items.summary: A 71-year-old motorcyclist died at the scene after hitting a pothole on the Western Highway in Victoria's south-west. Victoria Police stated that the exact circumstances surrounding the crash are yet to be determined.
items.title: 71-year-old motorcyclist dies after hitting pothole on Western Highway in Victoria

key_points: Social media users reported encountering 'high load' and 'regret' errors while attempting to book train tickets for Diwali and Chhath Puja travel to Bihar.
The East Central Railway announced a schedule of 16 festival special trains running between September 16 and November 30 to facilitate travel from major cities to Bihar.
These special services operate on daily, weekly, and biweekly bases connecting Delhi, Chandigarh, and other hubs to stations like Patna, Muzaffarpur, and Sitamarhi.
items.summary: Passengers on social media platforms reported significant difficulties booking train tickets for the upcoming Diwali and Chhath Puja festivals, particularly for travel to Bihar. Many users logged into the IRCTC app to find 'high load' or 'regret' messages, while waiting lists for some trains exceeded 200 entries. In response to these complaints, the East Central Railway announced a schedule of 16 festival special trains designed to ease travel between major cities and Bihar stations. These services, including routes from Delhi to Sitamarhi and Chandigarh to Patna, will operate between September 16 and November 30 on daily, weekly, and biweekly bases.
items.title: Passengers face booking errors during Diwali, Railways launch special trains to Bihar

key_points: Author Chandan Gowda argues that colonial India's development model was rooted in the belief that Indian society was backward and needed to emulate the industrial West.
Gowda states that Mysore's pursuit of modernity was driven by a desire for recognition and a conviction that the future lay elsewhere, specifically in Western models.
The interviewee notes that while the Wadiyar kings left significant imprints like the KRS Dam and IISc, they failed to create a local business community to sustain industrialization.
Gowda explains that the choice of Bengaluru for public sector units was strategic, influenced by Nehru's vision and the earlier pro-industry outlook of Diwan Visvesvaraya.
items.summary: In an interview with The Federal, Chandan Gowda discusses his new book, Longing for an Elsewhere, which explores how colonial ideas of backwardness shaped Mysore's development. Gowda, a professor at Vidyashilp University, argues that the region's modernity was driven by a desire to emulate the West rather than indigenous evolution. He explains that the Wadiyar kings and Diwan Visvesvaraya established key institutions like the Indian Institute of Science and the KRS Dam, yet failed to cultivate a local entrepreneurial class. Consequently, the state remained the primary agent of capital investment. Gowda suggests that while these efforts laid a foundation, the lack of a private business sector limited long-term industrial growth. He also highlights how Nehru strategically chose Bengaluru for public sector units, building on the earlier pro-industry vision of the Mysore elite.
items.title: Chandan Gowda explains how colonial ideas shaped Mysore's development

key_points: Chinese President Xi Jinping called on expanded BRICS members and partner countries to maintain stable and unimpeded industrial and supply chains during disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, according to state-run news agency Xinhua.

Speaking at the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit in New Delhi, Xi emphasized the role of the Global South in driving multipolarity and urged reforms to multilateral institutions and international financial architecture.
items.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping addressed the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit in New Delhi on September 13, 2026, urging expanded members and partner nations to keep supply chains stable despite shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. According to state-run news agency Xinhua, Xi highlighted the Global South's role in promoting multipolarity and called for reforms to multilateral institutions and international financial architecture to enhance developing countries' representation. He also proposed initiatives in science, technology, and artificial intelligence to foster integrated markets and practical cooperation among the "greater BRICS".
items.title: Xi urges BRICS partners to stabilize supply chains amid regional conflict

key_points: The UN passed a non-binding resolution endorsing the Equal Earth Projection to minimize the size distortions found in the traditional Mercator Projection.
Cartographers Jack Swab and Derek Alderman explain that while the new projection offers a fairer view of landmasses, it remains unsuitable for navigation purposes.
The United States was the only nation to vote against the resolution, citing concerns over language linking map distortions to colonial legacies.
items.summary: The United Nations passed a non-binding resolution endorsing the Equal Earth Projection, a map design intended to fairly represent the true size of Earth's landmasses. Cartographers Jack Swab and Derek Alderman explain that while this projection minimizes distortions that make Africa appear smaller than it is, the traditional Mercator projection remains useful for navigation. The UN resolution did not force adoption but endorsed the message that Equal Earth provides a fairer perspective for education and policy. The United States was the only country to vote against the proposal, objecting to language connecting map distortions to colonial legacies. African nations argue the change promotes cognitive justice by correcting the mental map of global leaders.
items.title: UN endorses Equal Earth map to correct Africa's size distortion

key_points: Researchers interviewed 530 people across five African nations who found existing climate services often lack local detail and fail to connect with Indigenous knowledge.
Participants stated that 91% of new services must integrate local forecasting methods and that information delivery channels need to include mobile phones and community radio.
The study concludes that governments and funders must finance ongoing collaboration between scientists and local users rather than simply purchasing final climate products.
items.summary: Researchers studying ecosystem restoration in Ghana, Kenya, Tanzania, Madagascar, and South Africa report that local users require climate services blending scientific data with Indigenous knowledge. The team interviewed 530 participants from diverse organizations, finding that while many use current forecasts, over 80% noted significant limitations regarding accessibility and relevance. Respondents emphasized a need for hyper-local information on land and water resources, delivered through trusted community networks. The authors state that institutions must fund the collaborative process of developing these services, ensuring they reflect local realities and support practical decision-making for climate adaptation.
items.title: Africa users demand local climate services blending science with Indigenous knowledge

key_points: A 46-year-old man chased a suspect wielding a knife after a carjacking in Sydney's south-west, helping to subdue the man on a busy road.
Police charged the 36-year-old suspect with aggravated robbery and other offences after the incident left two children with minor injuries.
items.summary: Nicholas Karagiannis, a 46-year-old witness, intervened in a carjacking in Sydney's south-west where a man allegedly armed with a knife fled with two young children. Police charged the 36-year-old suspect with aggravated robbery and reckless wounding after the incident. The children suffered minor injuries and were expected to be released from hospital on Sunday. Inspector Mark Wakeham praised the bravery of bystanders who assisted police during the pursuit.
items.title: Sydney Witness Intervenes in Carjacking Involving Two Young Boys

key_points: US captain Breanna Stewart emphasized that the team is turning the page on their previous Olympic loss to France.
France coach Jean-Aimé Toupane stated that winning gold would be a seismic shift for French basketball.
items.summary: The United States and France are scheduled to face each other in the women's FIBA World Cup final on Sunday. France defeated host Germany in the semifinals, while the four-time defending champion United States beat Spain. US captain Breanna Stewart noted that more than half the roster is new compared to the Olympic team that lost to France two years ago. Despite the history, Stewart said the team is focused on winning gold in Berlin. French players also downplayed the previous Olympic contest, focusing on the current match. France coach Jean-Aimé Toupane remarked that a gold medal would signal significant improvement in French basketball globally. This final marks France's best World Cup finish since 1953.
items.title: US and France set for women's FIBA World Cup final rematch

key_points: Iranian officials said Iran and Oman agreed on new entry and exit routes for the Strait of Hormuz after intensive talks.
items.summary: Iranian officials reported that Iran and Oman have finalized new entry and exit routes for the Strait of Hormuz following intensive diplomatic talks. A source close to Iran's negotiating team told the semi-official Tasnim news agency the agreement was reached in late August. Under the understanding, the Gulf's entry route lies entirely within Iran's territorial waters, and a portion of the exit route also falls within Iranian waters. The source stated the route will operate under Iranian arrangements and the southern route will close once the new system becomes operational, noting the United States had insisted the southern route must remain open.
items.title: Iran and Oman agree new Strait of Hormuz shipping routes

key_points: Prime Minister Narendra Modi paused his BRICS Summit opening remarks to ask a translator if Chinese President Xi Jinping was okay after noticing him look uncomfortable. The incident, captured on Doordarshan, showed Modi's personal concern for the Chinese leader during their first meeting in seven years.
items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi paused his BRICS Summit opening remarks to ask a translator if Chinese President Xi Jinping was okay after noticing him look uncomfortable. The incident, captured on Doordarshan, showed Modi's personal concern for the Chinese leader during their first meeting in seven years. Xi Jinping later skipped the gala dinner due to fatigue, though no official reaction from China explained the earlier discomfort. While the two leaders shared warm handshakes and a huddle with Vladimir Putin, border disputes remain a significant issue in their bilateral relations.
items.title: PM Modi pauses BRICS speech after noticing Xi Jinping appeared uncomfortable

key_points: Vedant Gupte of Trackk stated that the selling was driven by global factors rather than domestic concerns, while analysts warn that ongoing geopolitical tensions could further influence investor sentiment.
items.summary: Foreign Portfolio Investors withdrew 13,138 crore from Indian equities in the first half of September, according to data from the Central Depository Services (India) Ltd. The outflow followed a period of net buying in July and August but was driven by heightened global uncertainty, rising crude oil prices, and strong U.S. bond yields. Vedant Gupte, Co-Founder and CEO of Trackk, noted that the selling was primarily a dollar-and-crude story rather than an India-specific issue. Analysts suggest that ongoing geopolitical tensions, particularly the Iran-U.S. conflict, may continue to influence FPI flows. Additionally, foreign investors extended their selling to the debt market during the same period.
items.title: FPIs withdraw 13,138 crore from Indian equities in September amid global uncertainty

key_points: Modi stated that India's presidency has transformed the shared vision of resilience, innovation, cooperation, and sustainability into a win-win collaboration.
The summit will feature bilateral meetings with leaders from seven nations, including South Africa, Kazakhstan, and the Philippines.
items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed international leaders at the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi on Sunday, where the event focused on resilience, innovation, cooperation, and sustainability. News agency ANI reported that Modi greeted Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, Saudi Arabia's Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud, and other dignitaries with handshakes. Addressing the open session, Modi said India's presidency has transformed the shared vision into a win-win collaboration through these four pillars. He also highlighted the BRICS Network on Digital Agriculture to support farmers using AI and geospatial technology. The summit continues with scheduled bilateral meetings involving leaders from seven nations, including South Africa and Kazakhstan.
items.title: PM Modi hosts BRICS leaders, outlines four pillars for global growth

key_points: Ritabrata Banerjee said his group wants Mamata Banerjee elected from Nandigram and would withdraw its nominee even if she runs as an independent candidate.
items.summary: The Trinamool Congress faction led by Ritabrata Banerjee announced it will not field a candidate for the Nandigram Assembly bye-poll if party chief Mamata Banerjee contests the seat, The Hindu reported. Ritabrata Banerjee stated his group prefers Mamata Banerjee to be elected from Nandigram and would withdraw its nominee even if she runs as an independent candidate. The statement follows a meeting between the Election Commission and representatives of the two TMC factions regarding their claims to the party's name and electoral symbol.
items.title: TMC rebels vow to withdraw Nandigram candidate if Mamata Banerjee contests

key_points: Leomi White of Activate Rawmarsh stated that families cannot keep up with expenses, noting one parent pays £6 daily for a breakfast club to work.
items.summary: A charity in Chancellor John Healey's constituency reports that working families earning just above benefit thresholds are struggling with the cost of living. Leomi White, project coordinator at Activate Rawmarsh, stated that these families receive no help despite working, with some paying £6 daily for breakfast clubs to afford employment. White urged the government to extend support to those living on a financial cliff-edge, noting that current schemes primarily assist those on benefits rather than working households.
items.title: Charity warns working families in Rawmarsh need more government help

key_points: Chennai-based artist K. Benitha Perciyal is presenting a solo exhibition titled 'How Long Will We Live? Or When Will We Die?' at Ashvita's flagship gallery from August 7 to September 30.
items.summary: Chennai-based artist K. Benitha Perciyal is presenting a solo exhibition titled 'How Long Will We Live? Or When Will We Die?' at Ashvita's flagship gallery from August 7 to September 30. The show features her collection of objects gathered over years, which she uses in a dense, layered process. In an interview, Perciyal explained that her practice involves gathering objects over years to create assemblages where natural materials disfigure and restore themselves during the drying process.
items.title: Artist K. Benitha Perciyal discusses her solo exhibition and creative process

key_points: On the second day of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi emphasised resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability as core pillars for the bloc's future growth.
items.summary: On the second day of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi emphasised resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability as core pillars for the bloc's future growth. He warned that the weaponisation of technology and critical minerals could hinder shared progress and called for inclusive supply chains that benefit the Global South.
items.title: PM Modi urges BRICS nations to build resilient supply chains and combat technology weaponisation

key_points: Cheryl Cottle-Hunkin warned that thousands of households relying on heating oil face severe financial pressure due to global tensions driving prices up.
Heating oil costs have surged from approximately 60p to 97p per litre, creating anxiety for families and impacting farming businesses across Devon and Cornwall.
A UK Government spokesperson stated that £53m is being provided to support heating oil users while duty on red diesel has been slashed to its lowest rate in over 20 years.
items.summary: Cheryl Cottle-Hunkin, a Devon County Council cabinet member, warned that rising global oil prices are creating significant financial anxiety for thousands of households relying on heating oil. She noted that prices have jumped from about 60p to 97p per litre following conflict in Iran, a spike that severely impacts both families and farming operations. While Cottle-Hunkin highlighted the lack of a price cap for heating oil compared to gas, a UK Government spokesperson confirmed direct action to protect consumers. This includes allocating £53m to support heating oil users and reducing red diesel duty to its lowest level in over two decades.
items.title: Rising oil prices create financial worry for households as winter approaches

key_points: The Place for People exhibition emerged during Indira Gandhi's Emergency era to reintroduce ordinary people into Indian art narratives.
Curator Geeta Kapur collaborated with mid-career and emerging artists to create a democratic intervention against abstract idealism.
items.summary: The Place for People exhibition emerged during Indira Gandhi's Emergency era to reintroduce ordinary people into Indian art narratives. Curator Geeta Kapur collaborated with mid-career and emerging artists to create a democratic intervention against abstract idealism. Works by Gulammohammed Sheikh, Bhupen Khakhar, and Vivan Sundaram depicted urban isolation and collective experiences through narrative figuration. The show positioned itself as a radical response to political silence, allowing artists to tell their own stories rather than serving as aesthetic arbiters. While not all participants studied at MSU Baroda, the exhibition unified diverse voices to interrogate India's plural public spaces and overlapping temporalities. Art critic Ranjit Hoskote later described the event as an exhibition-as-manifesto that rejected vacuous transcendentalism in favor of lived experience.
items.title: Artists reclaim people in Indian modernism exhibition Place for People

key_points: Tesco has reported to City of London police after unlicensed casinos used its branding in deceptive advertisements on Facebook and Instagram.
The fake casino website claimed to be official and referenced Tesco's history, yet it lacks the legal license required to operate gambling services in Great Britain.
Regulators including the Gambling Commission and Advertising Standards Authority are aware of the issue but have struggled to stop the spread of these ads.
items.summary: Tesco has alerted City of London police after becoming the latest victim of a scam involving unlicensed casinos advertising via Facebook and Instagram. The supermarket chain is among several household-name businesses targeted in an apparent effort by illegal operators to capitalise on brand recognition. A fake 'Tesco casino' was advertised on the platform until the Guardian contacted Meta, which subsequently removed the ads. The fraudulent site claimed to be official but does not hold a gambling license in Great Britain. While the Gambling Commission and Advertising Standards Authority are aware of the problem, they have had little success preventing the spread of these deceptive materials. Other companies, including Barclays and Monzo, have also reported similar misuse of their intellectual property by rogue gambling firms.
items.title: Tesco alerts police after unlicensed casinos hijack its brand in scam ads

key_points: RTI data reveals Indian Railways lost Rs.104.51 crore in linen between January 2022 and May 2026, with face towels being the most stolen item.
The author describes a cultural tendency to treat trains as extensions of home, leading passengers to inadvertently steal bedding and other public property.
The article notes that theft of public infrastructure like bridges and tracks is common, often harming railway attendants who bear the financial loss.
items.summary: Palash Krishna Mehrotra writes about the widespread theft of public property in India, highlighting a specific crisis involving Indian Railways. RTI data indicates that between January 2022 and May 2026, the railways lost Rs.104.51 crore in linen, including 41.13 lakh bedsheets and 46.54 lakh face towels. The author suggests this theft stems from a psychological tendency where passengers treat trains as extensions of their homes, leading to accidental or intentional removal of bedding. Beyond linen, the text details spectacular heists of bridges and engines, often executed in plain sight. Ultimately, Mehrotra argues that while the state loses little, the financial burden falls cruelly on railway attendants whose pay is docked for missing items.
items.title: Indian Railways loses billions in linen theft amid public property heists

key_points: Nepali hydropower worker Sanjay Sah survived 10 days trapped in a flooded tunnel after a catastrophic flood killed at least 1,429 people and left more than 5,640 missing.
items.summary: Nepali hydropower worker Sanjay Sah survived 10 days trapped in a flooded tunnel after a catastrophic flood killed at least 1,429 people and left more than 5,640 missing. Sah told AFP he survived through his Hindu faith and the hope of hearing another voice from nearby worker Kabir Maharjan while awaiting rescue on September 4.
items.title: Nepal tunnel survivor Sanjay Sah recalls 10-day ordeal after deadly flood

key_points: Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson faces a tight contest against Magdalena Andersson as Swedes head to the polls on Sunday.
items.summary: Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson and opposition leader Magdalena Andersson are battling for the premiership in a closely fought election. Kristersson has said he could form a governing coalition that formally includes the Sweden Democrats, which would mark a historic breakthrough for the far right. Around eight million people are eligible to vote, with more than half having already cast their ballots in advance.
items.title: Swedes vote in tight election as far right eyes historic breakthrough

key_points: May el-Toukhy's film Woman Unknown won the Golden Lion at the 83rd Venice Film Festival, marking a rare double victory with lead actress Mathilde Arcel also taking Best Actress.
items.summary: May el-Toukhy's drama Woman Unknown won the Golden Lion at the 83rd Venice Film Festival, making her the only woman to solely direct a film in the main competition this year. Lead actress Mathilde Arcel also won Best Actress for her role. The jury gave the Silver Lion to Possible Love and a special jury prize to the documentary NAZA, which received a record-breaking 25-minute standing ovation after its premiere.
items.title: Woman Unknown wins Golden Lion at Venice Film Festival

key_points: Carlos Sainz will start the Spanish Grand Prix 20th after the FIA penalized him three places for impeding Valtteri Bottas during qualifying.
items.summary: Carlos Sainz will start the Spanish Grand Prix 20th after receiving a three-place penalty for impeding Valtteri Bottas during Saturday's qualifying session. The FIA stated that Williams failed to inform Sainz about Bottas closing in, causing unnecessary impediment. Meanwhile, Formula One champion Lando Norris secured pole position for McLaren, beating Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli by 0.011 seconds at the Madrid circuit.
items.title: Carlos Sainz starts 20th after three-place penalty for impeding Bottas

key_points: The authors propose a model where intelligence and Polanyi knowledge combine to produce output, noting that recent U.S. intelligence shocks increase marginal returns in the Polanyi sector.
items.summary: The authors propose a model where intelligence and Polanyi knowledge combine to produce output, noting that recent U.S. intelligence shocks increase marginal returns in the Polanyi sector. The authors state that while transitional unemployment may occur in the intelligence sector, wage and employment gains in the Polanyi sector will arrive slowly over a long period. This framework suggests the Solow model fails to capture major AI-driven changes because it ignores these specific complementarities.
items.title: A simple model explains AI-aided economic growth

key_points: ACE Equity identified 11 penny stocks that recorded returns between 27% and 156% over the last six months.
items.summary: ACE Equity identified 11 penny stocks that recorded returns between 27% and 156% over the last six months. The screening criteria included a market capitalisation below Rs 1,000 crore, a share price under Rs 20, and a minimum trading volume of 5 lakh shares. These filters targeted low-priced, actively traded micro-cap stocks showing strong upward price momentum.
items.title: ACE Equity identifies 11 penny stocks with up to 156% gains in six months

key_points: The Nifty and Sensex closed lower on Friday, extending a three-month downturn amid global uncertainty.
Analysts Vinod Nair and Radhakrishnan warn that sustained crude prices above $100 and upcoming Fed decisions will weigh on sentiment.
Defensive sectors like healthcare outperformed while real estate lagged, with experts advising caution near the 23,000 support level.
items.summary: Indian equity markets declined on Friday, with the Nifty falling 0.34% to 23,398.10 and the Sensex dropping 0.16% to 74,781.76. The broader market extended its weakness as investors focused on the upcoming US Federal Reserve decision and persistent high crude oil prices. Vinod Nair of Geojit Investments noted that crude remaining above $100 per barrel due to West Asian hostilities remains a central factor driving negative sentiment. Radhakrishnan added that rising energy costs could widen India's import bill and squeeze corporate margins. While healthcare and pharma sectors led gains, real estate corrected sharply. Experts suggest the 23,000–23,300 zone offers key support for the Nifty, though technical structures remain fragile.
items.title: Indian markets fall as crude prices and Fed policy drive volatility

key_points: Japanese director Hirokazu Koreeda's film Look Back won five collateral awards at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival.
The Golden Lion for Best Film went to Woman Unknown by Danish director May el-Toukhy.
items.summary: At the 83rd Venice International Film Festival, Japanese director Hirokazu Koreeda's Look Back secured five collateral awards. The ceremony took place on Saturday night on the Lido island. While Koreeda's film was in competition for the Golden Lion, that top prize went to Woman Unknown by May el-Toukhy. Other independent awards included the Leoncino d'Oro for Shinya Tsukamoto's Nelson-san and the Cinema & Arts Award for Takashi Miike's Shumei.
items.title: Hirokazu Koreeda's Look Back Wins Five Collateral Awards at Venice

key_points: Ian Sample hosts a live Science Weekly episode featuring Michael Safi and Madeleine Finlay discussing the rise of AI psychosis.
The hosts examine cases where individuals claim to have made scientific breakthroughs using AI chatbots.
items.summary: In a live episode of Science Weekly recorded at the London podcast festival, Ian Sample hosts a discussion with Michael Safi and Madeleine Finlay about how artificial intelligence is reshaping human cognition. The group explores the phenomenon of 'AI psychosis,' examining cases where people believe they have made scientific breakthroughs or cured diseases using chatbots. The conversation highlights concerns regarding a technology now used by more than a billion people.
items.title: Guardian podcast explores AI psychosis and chatbot delusions

key_points: Prosper and Martine Assouline, editors of Assouline Publishing, describe their next book as weighing 176 pounds, costing 20,000 euros, and selling out in two minutes.
The couple stated that their publishing house offers no sales and accepts no returns, prioritizing quality over accessibility.
Prosper Assouline expressed certainty that physical books will endure despite digital trends, noting his Jewish heritage and the Torah as proof.
items.summary: Prosper and Martine Assouline, editors of Assouline Publishing, discussed their upcoming project with EL PAÍS, describing a future book that will weigh 176 pounds, cost 20,000 euros, and sell out in two minutes. The couple, who have published over 2,500 titles and operate 18 stores worldwide, emphasized that their high-end books are luxury objects designed to be displayed rather than read cover to cover. They noted that their most expensive book, a Jay-Z edition, sold for up to 163,000 dollars at auction. While acknowledging the luxury sector faces challenges, the publishers remain optimistic about the enduring value of physical books. Prosper Assouline stated he is certain that while digital media may disappear, the book will remain because he was born with a book, the Torah.
items.title: Assouline Publishers plan a 176-pound book selling for 20,000 euros

key_points: Orriols states that Ancient Egyptian society was actually modest, with human sex appearing only in rare, non-official representations.
The scholar interprets the Turin Erotic Papyrus as a mockery of hegemonic masculinity rather than a depiction of common practice.
items.summary: Egyptologist Marc Orriols argues that Hollywood and biased ancient accounts have distorted the perception of sex in Ancient Egypt. Speaking at the VIII congress at the Autonomous University of Barcelona, Orriols stated that the civilization was actually modest, with human sex appearing only in rare, non-official representations. He interprets the 3,150-year-old Turin Erotic Papyrus as a mockery of hegemonic masculinity rather than a depiction of common practice. Orriols noted that while religious iconography shows sexual fluidity, everyday life lacked such depictions, and concepts like non-binary identity or documented homosexuality did not exist in the formal culture.
items.title: Egyptologist Marc Orriols challenges Hollywood views of Ancient Egyptian sexuality

key_points: Emergency teams searched for over 30 people after the MV Matui sank in Vanuatu, leaving one person dead and 15 survivors accounted for.
items.summary: Emergency teams searched for more than 30 people after the MV Matui sank in Vanuatu, leaving at least one person dead and 15 survivors accounted for. Prime Minister Jotham Napat stated the disaster resulted from strong winds and unheeded marine warnings, possibly involving vessel overloading. The search shifted from open waters to the southeast coast where currents may have carried survivors.
items.title: One dead, 30 missing after ferry sinks in Vanuatu

key_points: The agency warned of large volcanic rocks within about 3 kilometers of the crater after volcanic activity intensified and the number of large volcanic earthquakes increased since Aug. 17.
items.summary: Japan's Meteorological Agency raised the eruption alert level for Mount Tokachidake in Hokkaido to Level 3 on Saturday morning, banning entry to the 2,077-meter mountain. This is the first time that Level 3 has been issued for the mountain since the alert system was introduced in 2008. The agency said volcanic activity has intensified, raising the possibility of an eruption and warning of large volcanic rocks within about 3 kilometers of the crater. The Kamifurano town government has issued an evacuation order for the Fukiage Onsen area and advised elderly and other vulnerable residents in the Tokachidake Onsen area to evacuate.
items.title: Japan raises volcanic alert for Hokkaido's Mt. Tokachidake to Level 3

key_points: The article reports that Russian men are considering exile instead of being sent to a war with no end in sight.
items.summary: The article reports that Russian men are considering exile instead of being sent to a war with no end in sight. It quotes a citizen stating that ordinary people do not want to be sent to such a conflict.
items.title: Russian men consider exile rather than joining an endless war

key_points: Reed contends that independent AI safety reviews are standard operational practices rather than emergency measures for existential threats.
The author argues that current AI models lack the independent operation capabilities required to pose an extinction risk.
Reed warns that media hysteria and political pressure may replace thoughtful debate about actual AI safety concerns.
items.summary: Reed argues that the recent surge in AI safety concerns is largely a media-driven narrative rather than a reflection of immediate existential threats. He suggests that proposals for independent AI reviews address standard commercial needs like operational excellence and interpretability. Reed points out that current AI models cannot operate independently on small devices, meaning humans can simply unplug them if necessary. He notes that frontier labs invest billions in massive data centers because they assume AI will require significant computing power for years. The author concludes that while real AI risks exist, the fear of human extinction is unlikely as long as an off switch remains available. Reed warns that the biggest danger now is hysteria replacing thoughtful debate in Washington and Brussels.
items.title: Reed argues AI extinction fears are exaggerated and media hype is dangerous
